chunks.arabic_text: عَنِ ٱلْإِمَامِ عَلِيٍّ، عَنِ ٱلْمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَىٰ، عَنِ ٱلْيُونُسِ، عَنِ ٱلْجَمِيلِ، عَنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: From Imam Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: يَغْدُو ٱلنَّاسُ عَلَىٰ ثَلَاثَةِ أَصْنَافٍ: عَالِمٍ، وَمُتَعَلِّمٍ، وَغَثَاءٍ، فَنَحْنُ ٱلْعُلَمَاءُ، وَشِيعَتُنَا ٱلْمُتَعَلِّمُونَ، وَسَائِرُ ٱلنَّاسِ غَثَاءٌ

translations.en: I heard him saying: The people rise up (every morning) being in one of three categories: a knowledgeable scholar, a student seeking knowledge, or scum. So we are the scholars, and our Shia are the students, and the rest of the people are scum.

en.summary: The Imam categorizes humanity into three groups based on their relationship with religious knowledge: the scholars (who possess knowledge), the students (who seek it), and the 'scum' (the general populace who are neither). This hadith establishes a theological hierarchy where the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers occupy the esteemed positions of knowledge and learning.
en.seo_question: What are the three categories of people according to this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?

key_terms.غَثَاءٍ: Scum/General populace (those who are neither scholars nor students)
